newsitem.title: USA: Samsung Electronics complete AST Research merger.
newsitem.headline: Samsung Electronics complete AST Research merger.

text.p: Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. said Monday it completed buying the 54 percent of computer maker AST Research Inc. it did not already own for $170 million.

Samsung, the Korean maker of semiconductors and personal computers, plans to revamp the development and manufacturing operations of ailing AST to make it one of the world's top five PC makers by 2005, the company said.

Samsung, a long-time investor in AST, announced in April it would pay $170 million for the 54 percent stake it did not already own. The company paid $5.40 a share for 28.54 million tendered -- about 90 percent of the 31 million shares outstanding. An AST spokesman said Samsung expects to pay a total of $170 million when all the shares are tendered.

AST, once one of the biggest PC makers in the world, fell on hard times three years ago because of poor product development and marketing and fierce competition against bigger rivals such as Compaq Computer Corp.
The Irvine, Calif., company will operate as a wholly owned Samsung Electronics subsidiary.
